Test Steps: Per alert: inject triggering condition then verify || Alert 1 (5xx >1%): kill DB RW → write errors → 5xx >1% | Record T_inject T_alert | Alert latency = difference || Alert 2 (latency breach): inject 2s DB latency | Record T_inject T_alert || Alert 3 (pods <75%): kill 2 of 4 | Record || Alert 4 (Kafka drops): kill Kafka during writes | Record || For each: verify fires + auto-resolves
Verification Steps: V1. Per alert: T_alert - T_inject (detection latency) | V2. Did it fire? (false negative if not) | V3. False positives during baseline? | V4. Alert metadata: service + endpoint + severity + value | V5. Auto-resolve after fault removed?
Expected Outcome: Each fires within defined window (1-5 min) | Zero false negatives | Actionable metadata included | Auto-resolves within 2 min of removal | Alert latency <3 min for critical
Pass Criteria: [PASS] All alerts fire within window | [PASS] Zero false negatives | [PASS] Auto-resolve after removal | [PASS] Metadata actionable | [FAIL] ANY alert doesn't fire | [FAIL] Latency >10 min | [FAIL] Doesn't auto-resolve
Customer Impact: If alerts don't fire during failures ops doesn't know service broken. Customers report before monitoring. Alert failure = reactive not proactive.
IMF Evidence: EIMF-494 (NPA SRP 5xx 100% for 12+ HOURS) | EIMF-497 (DLP alerts didn't fire for 6hrs on duplicate IP issue) — if alerts don't fire ops learns from customers not dashboards

Scenario: Grey-box correlation — full pipeline match
Preconditions: BL-01 baseline | DB+Redis+Kafka+Prometheus access | k6 with correlation_id in every request
Test Steps: 1. Start k6: 50 req/s mixed 30 min — each request has unique correlation_id | 2. k6 logs every: correlation_id + operation + result + timestamp | 3. POST records config_id from 201 | 4. After 30 min stop | 5. DB verify: every 201 POST has row + every 200 DELETE has no row | 6. Redis verify: recent GETs have cache entries | 7. Kafka verify: CUD count vs event count | 8. Prometheus verify: counter total vs k6 total
Verification Steps: V1. DB: 2xx POST → row exists (100%) | V2. DB: 2xx DELETE → row absent (100%) | V3. Kafka: CUD count vs events (≥99%) | V4. Prometheus: total vs k6 (100%) | V5. Drift count per layer | V6. Identify which layer drifts
Expected Outcome: DB 100% match | Kafka ≥99% | Prometheus 100% | Total drift <1% | Zero: 2xx with no DB row (data loss) | Zero: non-2xx with DB row (phantom)
Pass Criteria: [PASS] DB correlation 100% | [PASS] Kafka ≥99% | [PASS] Prometheus 100% | [PASS] Zero phantom writes | [FAIL] ANY 2xx no DB row (P0 data loss) | [FAIL] ANY non-2xx with row (phantom write) | [FAIL] Kafka <95%
Customer Impact: API returns 200 but DB row missing = data loss. DB row exists but Kafka event missing = endpoint never gets update. Grey-box catches silent failures.
Tooling: k6 (correlation IDs) + DB + Redis CLI + kafka-consumer + Prometheus
IMF Evidence: IMF-1348 (delay in RTP config sync) | EIMF-28 (Fed config sync not working) — grey-box catches DB↔Kafka↔downstream drift that API-only testing misses

Scenario: 72-hour soak + periodic chaos
Preconditions: BL-01 baseline all metrics documented | Environment reserved 3+ days | Chaos schedule configured | Grafana long-term dashboards
Test Steps: 1. Start k6: 50 req/s 70:30 R:W sustain 72 hours | 2. Record all metrics at T+0 | 3. Chaos schedule every 4 hours rotating: H4 Redis restart | H8 pod kill | H12 DB slow 500ms 2min | H16 Kafka restart | H20 Redis restart | H24 pod kill | ...repeat (18 faults total) | 4. After each: record recovery + verify baseline return | 5. Every 4hr: snapshot goroutines+heap+connections+FDs+latency+errors | 6. At T+72: stop record final | 7. Compare T+0 vs T+72 slope analysis | 8. Plot per-fault recovery over 72hr (later recoveries slower?)
Verification Steps: V1. Per-fault recovery time (consistent not growing) | V2. 72hr trends: goroutines slope≈0 + heap oscillating + FDs flat + pool stable + GC stable | V3. Per-fault comparison: fault-1 vs fault-18 recovery | V4. Error rate trend: <0.1% outside fault windows | V5. Latency at T+72 vs T+0 ±10%
Expected Outcome: Zero cumulative degradation: T+72 within 10% of T+0 | Every fault self-heals per individual benchmarks | No recovery regression (fault-18 ≤ fault-1) | No leaks: near-zero slope all metrics | No OOMKills in 72hr | Latency stable | Error rate <0.1% outside faults
